comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C55-C57 regarding control experiments showing phage-specific effects. Both evaluations find the data convincing that the phage-antibiotic trade-off is not universal, with OpenEval noting the phage genus-specific nature and peer reviewers accepting these findings without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C58-C71 regarding genomic analysis and evolutionary trajectories. Both evaluations strongly support the mutational findings, with OpenEval providing detailed analysis of strain-specific patterns and peer reviewers highlighting this as a novel contribution that improves understanding of the mechanism.

Perfect agreement on claims C72-C86 regarding RNA-seq transcriptional changes. Both evaluations find the data convincing, with OpenEval noting consistency with mutational data and peer reviewers acknowledging this supports the observed phenotypic changes in virulence properties.

Perfect agreement on claims C87-C95 regarding reduced hemolytic activity and biofilm formation. Both evaluations support these virulence phenotype findings, with OpenEval noting strain-specific effects and peer reviewers finding the experiments convincing.

Perfect agreement on claims C96-C98 regarding reduced clumping/fibrinogen binding. Both evaluations find the data convincing, with OpenEval noting consistency with transcriptomic data and peer reviewers specifically mentioning this as a convincing phenotypic change.

Perfect agreement on claims C99-C106 regarding evolutionary dynamics under dual selection. Both evaluations support the checkerboard assay findings showing strain-specific responses and the balance of selective pressures, with no concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C107-C110 regarding main conclusions. Both evaluations strongly support the overall findings, with OpenEval emphasizing the convergent phenotypes from divergent genetics and peer reviewers finding the study complete and convincing with novel contributions.

Strong agreement on claims C32-C36 (OpenEval R1) overlapping with C32-C36, C39-C40, C41-C43 (Peer R1). Both evaluations support the core phenotypic observations of phage activity and β-lactam sensitization. Peer review groups these with additional dose-response claims, while OpenEval separates them into distinct results.

Agreement on claims C37-C40 (OpenEval R2) with C39-C40 appearing in Peer R1. Both evaluations support the baseline resistance and specific loss following phage treatment. OpenEval focuses specifically on MIC data and controls, while peer review groups this with broader phenotypic observations.

Agreement on claims C41-C43 regarding dose-response relationships. OpenEval provides detailed analysis noting strain-specific variability in LAC, while peer reviewers group this with other core phenotypic findings and find all experiments convincing.

Strong agreement on claims C44-C48 regarding Evo2 characterization. Both evaluations support the evolved phage findings, with OpenEval providing detailed analysis of plaquing, lytic activity, and genomic data, while peer reviewers specifically note the enhanced virulence demonstration.

Partial agreement on Evo2 effects. OpenEval R5 covers C49-C51 (β-lactam sensitization and occasional other antibiotic effects), while Peer R2 includes C49 along with broader Evo2 characterization. OpenEval notes inconsistency in non-β-lactam effects across replicates.

Agreement on claims C50-C51 regarding occasional sensitization to non-β-lactam antibiotics. OpenEval notes these are inconsistent secondary effects, while peer reviewers accept these as exceptions to the general pattern without challenge.

Agreement on claims C52-C54 regarding clinical isolates. OpenEval R6 focuses on extending findings to recent clinical strains with detailed MIC and plaquing data, while Peer R2 groups this with broader Evo2 findings and notes it increases translational relevance.
